method_card.title: How to Find the nth Term of a Sequence
steps: Find the common difference d between consecutive terms.
The rule is dn + (first term minus d). Check it at n = 1.
Geometric sequences multiply by a ratio r: nth term = ar^(n−1).
For a term from a sum rule Sₙ, the nth term is Sₙ − Sₙ₋₁.
method_card.content:
Arithmetic sequences have a constant difference \(d\). The nth term is \(dn + (\text{first term} - d)\): find \(d\), subtract it from the first term for the constant, then check \(n = 1\) rebuilds the start.

Geometric sequences multiply by a constant ratio \(r\); the nth term is \(ar^{n-1}\).

To test membership, set the nth term equal to the number and solve: a whole-number position means it is in the sequence.

Special sequences: squares 1, 4, 9, 16; cubes 1, 8, 27; triangular 1, 3, 6, 10.
method_card.example:
Find the nth term of 5, 8, 11, 14, ...

\(d = 3\); constant \(= 5 - 3 = 2\); nth term \(= 3n + 2\). Check \(n = 1\): \(3 + 2 = 5\) \(\checkmark\)

bronze.title: Bronze: the nth term of a straight-line sequence
steps: Find the common difference d: subtract each term from the next. If it is the same every time, the sequence is arithmetic.
The rule starts dn. Find the constant from the zero term: first term minus d.
So nth term = dn + (first term minus d). Always check it at n = 1 rebuilds the start.

silver.title: Silver: membership, falling sequences, and geometric
steps: To test if a number N is in a sequence, find the nth term, set it equal to N and solve for n. A whole number means yes; a fraction means no.
Falling sequences have a negative d, but the rule is still dn + (first term minus d).
Geometric sequences multiply by a fixed ratio r each time; the nth term is \(ar^{n-1}\).

gold.title: Gold: sums, series, and finding an unknown
steps: For a term from a sum rule \(S_n\), the nth term is \(S_n - S_{n-1}\): work out both totals and subtract.
A geometric series adds the terms; list them and add carefully, keeping fractions exact.
If three terms are arithmetic, the gaps are equal: middle minus first = last minus middle. Solve that for the unknown.
